question: What are the names of pilots who have planes in both Austin and Boston?
statements: CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE "pilots" AS SELECT "pn" AS "pn", "pln" AS "pln", "age" AS "age" FROM table_1;

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE "plane_locations" AS WITH src AS (
    SELECT * FROM table_2
),
-- Unpivot the wide columns into rows: plane_col and city value
unpivoted AS (
    SELECT 'b_1_bomber'   AS plane_col, CAST(b_1_bomber AS TEXT)   AS city FROM src
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'b_52_bomber'  AS plane_col, CAST(b_52_bomber AS TEXT)  AS city FROM src
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'f_14_fighter' AS plane_col, CAST(f_14_fighter AS TEXT) AS city FROM src
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'piper_cub'    AS plane_col, CAST(piper_cub AS TEXT)    AS city FROM src
),
-- Normalize city strings
norm AS (
    SELECT plane_col, LOWER(TRIM(city)) AS city_lc
    FROM unpivoted
    WHERE city IS NOT NULL
),
-- Determine presence flags per plane_col
flags AS (
    SELECT 
        plane_col,
        MAX(CASE WHEN city_lc = 'austin' THEN '1' ELSE NULL END)  AS austin,
        MAX(CASE WHEN city_lc = 'boston' THEN '1' ELSE NULL END)  AS boston
    FROM norm
    GROUP BY plane_col
),
-- Map plane_col keys to human-readable plane_name values expected to match pilots.pln
mapped AS (
    SELECT 
        CASE plane_col
            WHEN 'b_1_bomber'   THEN 'B-1 Bomber'
            WHEN 'b_52_bomber'  THEN 'B-52 Bomber'
            WHEN 'f_14_fighter' THEN 'F-14 Fighter'
            WHEN 'piper_cub'    THEN 'Piper Cub'
            ELSE plane_col
        END AS plane_name,
        austin,
        boston
    FROM flags
)
SELECT plane_name, austin, boston
FROM mapped

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE conductor_s_execution AS
WITH norm AS (
    SELECT
        p.pn AS pilot_name,
        p.pln AS plane_name,
        COALESCE(pl.austin, '') AS austin_val,
        COALESCE(pl.boston, '') AS boston_val
    FROM pilots p
    LEFT JOIN plane_locations pl
      ON LOWER(p.pln) = LOWER(pl.plane_name)
)
SELECT DISTINCT pilot_name
FROM norm
WHERE LENGTH(TRIM(austin_val)) > 0
  AND LENGTH(TRIM(boston_val)) > 0
ORDER BY pilot_name

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE conductor_s_execution AS
WITH cols AS (
    SELECT column_name
    FROM pragma_table_info('plane_locations')
    WHERE LOWER(column_name) NOT IN ('plane_name')
),
-- Build long table of plane -> city using UNION ALL over discovered columns
long AS (
    SELECT LOWER(REPLACE(REPLACE(c.column_name, ' ', '_'), '-', '_')) AS norm_plane,
           LOWER(TRIM(pl_val)) AS city
    FROM cols c,
    LATERAL (
        SELECT CAST(((SELECT plane_locations."' || c.column_name || '" FROM plane_locations WHERE LOWER(plane_name) IN ('location'))) AS VARCHAR) AS pl_val
    )
),
-- Above LATERAL with dynamic column isn't supported directly; instead, construct using DuckDB UNPIVOT
unpivoted AS (
    SELECT LOWER(REPLACE(REPLACE(col, ' ', '_'), '-', '_')) AS norm_plane,
           LOWER(TRIM(val)) AS city
    FROM (
        SELECT * FROM plane_locations WHERE TRUE
    )
    UNPIVOT(val FOR col IN (* EXCLUDE(plane_name)))
),
city_flags AS (
    SELECT norm_plane,
           MAX(CASE WHEN city = 'austin' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_austin,
           MAX(CASE WHEN city = 'boston' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_boston
    FROM unpivoted
    GROUP BY norm_plane
),
pilots_norm AS (
    SELECT pn AS pilot_name,
           LOWER(REPLACE(REPLACE(pln, ' ', '_'), '-', '_')) AS norm_plane
    FROM pilots
)
SELECT DISTINCT p.pilot_name
FROM pilots_norm p
JOIN city_flags f USING (norm_plane)
WHERE f.has_austin = 1 AND f.has_boston = 1
ORDER BY p.pilot_name

S:
# Unpivot plane_locations wide table where the first row (plane_name='location') holds the city per plane column,
# then find pilots whose plane is present in both Austin and Boston.

query = '''
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE conductor_s_execution AS
WITH unpivoted AS (
    SELECT LOWER(REPLACE(REPLACE(col, ' ', '_'), '-', '_')) AS norm_plane,
           LOWER(TRIM(val)) AS city
    FROM (
        SELECT * FROM plane_locations
    )
    UNPIVOT(val FOR col IN (* EXCLUDE(plane_name)))
    WHERE LOWER(plane_name) = 'location'
),
city_flags AS (
    SELECT norm_plane,
           MAX(CASE WHEN city = 'austin' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_austin,
           MAX(CASE WHEN city = 'boston' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_boston
    FROM unpivoted
    GROUP BY norm_plane
),
pilots_norm AS (
    SELECT pn AS pilot_name,
           LOWER(REPLACE(REPLACE(pln, ' ', '_'), '-', '_')) AS norm_plane
    FROM pilots
)
SELECT DISTINCT p.pilot_name
FROM pilots_norm p
JOIN city_flags f USING (norm_plane)
WHERE f.has_austin = 1 AND f.has_boston = 1
ORDER BY p.pilot_name
'''

db_api.execute_query(user_id, chat_id, query)
